_meta.source: TB_AI_Audit_Final_Detailed_Team_Final.md sec 8.2 (risk rating methodology), sec 3.2 (data sufficiency grading)
_meta.purpose: Atomic-rule weights for the composite risk score, and the mapping-coverage thresholds that decide confidence wording.
_meta.extraction_note: Weights generated from the Python literal by AST read. The two mapping-confidence thresholds were previously defined only inside build_data_sufficiency_grade; build_risk_indicators had no equivalent and reported a hardcoded 'Unknown'. Both tools now read these, so they cannot drift.
_meta.amend_policy: A score is the SUM of every triggered rule's weight, capped at 100. Bands: >75 Critical, >=50 High, >=25 Medium, else Low. Raising one weight shifts the whole population across bands -- change deliberately, and re-run the acceptance set afterwards.
_meta.provision_movement_anomaly_weight_note: 80, not ~15-25 like every other rule here, is deliberate: build_exception_consolidator's _process_risk_indicator_exceptions only reads risk_indicators.json's critical_risks list (score >75) -- high_risks/medium_risks are computed but never promoted into a finding. Verified against a real EPIL re-run: the flagship missed-risk example (a doubtful-debt provision, opening->closing -681.7%) scored only 20 (Low band) at weight 20 and never surfaced as a finding, reproducing the exact invisibility the client review flagged. This rule's own design intent (see risk.py's _apply_provision_movement_risks docstring) is 'audit-relevant by nature regardless of size' -- the same rationale SUSPENSE_CLEARING/INTERCOMPANY use at their current low weights, which this change does NOT touch or claim to fix; broadening critical_risks-only promotion to include high/medium risk accounts would fix this more generally but is a shared-function change affecting every rule here, out of scope for this fix.
